summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for chest pain described as pressure, concerning for acute coronary syndrome. He has a significant cardiac history including prior stents and non-STEMI. Evaluation revealed a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction with progression of coronary artery disease in the LAD, leading to percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stent placement and balloon angioplasty. Post-procedure, he remained chest pain-free with stable vital signs. His diabetes was managed with insulin, and metformin was resumed prior to discharge. Home medications for hypertension, heart failure, hyperlipidemia, and GERD were continued. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue dual antiplatelet therapy, monitor weight, and follow up with cardiology.
